source_of_truth: Read by hand in a Next.js App Router app. Every cross-module edge is legitimate: checkout imports catalog only through catalog/index.ts (the public entry); shared/money.ts is domain-free and only depended on BY domains (allowed direction); the middleware (shell) depends only on the auth domain, which is a default coreDomain the shell may use; the route lives at src/app/checkout/page.tsx so it classifies as the checkout domain and importing checkout is same-domain. No cross-module import targets a private file, no domain pair depends both ways (no cycle), no file is used by 3+ other domains (no hotspot). A correct auditor reports zero defect-level findings.

forbidden.why_not_a_defect: the middleware depends on auth, a default coreDomain; the shell is explicitly allowed to depend on core domains
catalog is a business domain importing shared/money.ts; this is a domain depending on shared code (allowed), not shared depending on a domain
checkout imports @/features/catalog, which resolves to catalog/index.ts (public entry), not a private file
